<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `25141ce88ebfb6f14a7d6c04b355e5fe2b3d88d5` — the merge of head `64c2e410492c2d3037c4eabf8cf901ab71352e64` into base `c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 25141ce88ebfb6f14a7d6c04b355e5fe2b3d88d5 && git checkout 25141ce88ebfb6f14a7d6c04b355e5fe2b3d88d5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200 64c2e410492c2d3037c4eabf8cf901ab71352e64 && git checkout -B drift-repro c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200 && git merge --no-ff 64c2e410492c2d3037c4eabf8cf901ab71352e64

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c857a93ee42d0144b4643f49f899053ea099e200` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd13bf7808f0ce7e4833ff3a297a355e9d3d4471`
Local-runs: none

PR #23412, card #23403 (Tier H, governed by `docs/adr/**`). The head is the PR's current head, `bd13bf7808`. It merges main `5656c5638a` (which contains 7a, `dac99c2277`) into `59761d4a71`, and it replaced `59761d4a71` while this review ran (dev comment 6162563147).

- The net diff, `origin/main...bd13bf7808` (merge base `5656c5638a`), is 8 files, +54 / −142.
- Its content matches `e4ec6ec1a5..59761d4a71` exactly; only the index lines and hunk offsets differ.
- The merge ref `18ff991d38` has the same tree as the head (empty diff).

Read for this record: card #23403, its claim 6161966159 and the dev report 6162484475; on #22975, the seat's answers 6161961558 and 8-post's report 6161864889; the PR body and its `## 维护者速读（草稿）` section; `a581c57eae`; and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The gate: holds.**

- **Unreachable on `main`.** `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` returned at once for any object other than `sys_position_permission_set`.
  - Stage 8 (`66949b7729`) deleted `objects/sys-position-permission-set.object.ts` and dropped it from `objects/index.ts`. The only definition left on `main` is `__tests__/legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.ts`.
  - The engine's `insert` and `update` both call `resolveObjectName` before `executeWithMiddleware`. That call throws `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for a name the registry does not hold (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`). So no write to that object reaches the security middleware, and none reaches the gate.
- **Removed cleanly.**
  - Removed: the call in the middleware, the method, its three unit cases, and the two imports only it used.
  - The three cases called the private method directly through `(plugin as any)`, so they stayed green while the gate was dead.
  - On the merge ref, `describeAnchorForbiddenBits` and `AnchorBindingContext` have no use left in `security-plugin.ts`. `readDeclaredCapabilityContext` (still used by `declareEveryone`), `PermissionDeniedError` and `bootstrapPermissionSets` are still used.
  - A `git grep` of the merged tree finds no code caller and no anchor JSON. Only prose names the gate now (finding B).
  - Side effect, harmless: `assertPackageManagedWriteGate`'s docblock now sits directly above its own method. Before, the anchor gate sat between them.
- **No ADR-0090 D9 guarantee is lost.** The gate judged `sys_position_permission_set` rows, and no grant reader reads that table.
  - The guest's grants come from the `guest` position's catalog definition: `resolveGuestAnchorGrants` calls `positionBoundSetNames` in `core/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`.
  - **`everyone`:** `describeAnchorForbiddenBits` runs in two places. `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` refuses with a 403, and `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` withholds on every derivation. `declareEveryone` filters the baseline with `describeHighPrivilegeBits`, which is the `everyone` tier exactly (`high-privilege.ts`).
  - **`guest`:** nothing on `main` calls the guest tier, and no door binds a set to `guest` (the anchors' seal, plus the refusal of a `guest` row on confirm). So the tier holds only because nothing can bind. Follow-up F4 (the bind door) must call it.

**2. The ADR edits: true of `main`, except one sentence (finding A).**

- **ADR-0138.** Edited: :171, item 4 (:372), item 5's re-read note (:400–402), and the enforcement-map row (:584).
  - All four are true of `main`. At `7b926f7600` the gate existed and called the predicate (`security-plugin.ts` :7080 and :7135 there).
  - D3 item 4's rule is unchanged: a set bound to `guest` must pass the strictest tier, and the item still ends "Unchanged."
  - The map row's status changes from `enforced` to `enforced for everyone; guest: follow-up F4`. That is an honest downgrade, consistent with F4 (:843) and with the row above it. It changes a status in the accepted record. It does not change a decision.
  - Form: the edits replace text in place, with no date, though each names its source (#15204 stage 8, #23403). `a581c57eae` instead made pure insertions (36 inserts, 0 replacements, dated notes).
  - I accept the in-place form for this ADR: its enforcement map is a living status table, and item 5's note is the 2026-10-14 amendment's own text. But no `Amended` segment or date records the change. Non-blocking.
- **ADR-0094.** Edited: :19, :187 and :399. All three are true.
  - Stage 7a deleted `permission-set-projection.ts` and its suite; both are absent on `main`.
  - Stage 8 removed the wiring: the `66949b7729` hunk in `security-plugin.ts` drops `registerPermissionSetProjection` and `reconcilePermissionSetProjection`.
  - `registerMutationProjector` remains (`protocol.ts` :6736).
  - The banner edit completes `a581c57eae`'s own dated RETIRED banner, which had predicted the deletion ("stays in the tree until stage 7a deletes it").
- **ADR-0126 (:97).** A dated path note in the same form as the existing one at :103. True, and an insertion.
- **ADR-0131 (:66 and :1008).** Dated insertions, and true.
  - At `2514d49f3` there were five bootstrap seeders. Each one's deletion is confirmed:

    | Seeder | Deleted by | Commit |
    |---|---|---|
    | `bootstrap-builtin-positions.ts` | stage 6a | `990341a93c` |
    | `bootstrap-declared-positions.ts` | stage 6a | `990341a93c` |
    | `bootstrap-system-capabilities.ts` | stage 6b-1b | `7aa8d51c0f` |
    | `bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts` | stage 6b-1c | `95a843573a` |
    | `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts` | stage 6b-2 | `c8a9783eca` |

  - `tenant-layer.ts`, `per-organization-catalog.ts` and `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` are present on `main`, as the note says.
  - The :1008 note names exactly the four seeders that appear in that code list.
- **ADR-0103 (:50–59).**
  - The correction itself is right. `SYSTEM_ROW_PROVENANCE` holds only `sys_position` and `sys_capability`, and `sharing-rule-provenance.ts` stamps an edited row `customized` instead of refusing it.
  - But the edit adds one sentence that is false of `main` (finding A). The aside is also rewritten in place, with no date.
- **ADR prose still naming a retired module, outside this card's five ADRs** (`a581c57eae` missed these too):
  - **ADR-0068 :3**, the Status line: "built-in identity rows seeded (`bootstrap-builtin-positions.ts`)". Stage 6a deleted that file, the boot writes no `sys_position` row, and the line has no `Amended` segment.
  - **ADR-0086 :71** cites `objects/sys-permission-set.object.ts` as true "today". Borderline: its Status line's `Amended` segment covers the retirement.
  - I grepped `docs/adr` on the head for every file 6a, 6b, 8, 7b and 7a deleted. Every other hit is dated, carries a note, or sits in ADR-0131 D13's list of retirements.

**3. Gates: green on the head.**

- `check:adr-symbol-anchors`: the `Lint · docs & code guards` step "ADR symbol anchors resolve (no line numbers survive)" succeeded.
- `check:adr-links`: the `Check Documentation Links` step "Check ADR cross-links" succeeded.
- `check:adr-anchors`: step 9 of `Lint · repo & tooling gates` succeeded.
- The only symbol anchor that named the gate (ADR-0138 :171) is gone. Both anchors left on the changed lines still resolve: `high-privilege.ts#describeAnchorForbiddenBits` (:192) and `delegated-admin-gate.ts#ANCHOR_POSITIONS` (:151).

**4. The 速读 draft: true of the diff, except for the gaps below.**

- 「让每一处都与 main 当前行为一致」 is not true while finding A stands.
- 「不改变任何决定」 holds for decisions. But the draft does not say that the enforcement map moves the guest tier from `enforced` to follow-up F4. It says only that no door binds a set to `guest`, which is the substance.
- 「约 120 行」 is fine: 124 lines of code are deleted.
- Outside the 速读, the body's Verification section is stale. It still reads "On `59761d4a71` … not re-merged", but the head is now the re-merge `bd13bf7808`, recorded only in comment 6162563147.

**Findings**

- **A (blocking). ADR-0103 :53–54 is false of `main`.**
  - The sentence: "On `main` today only `sys_sharing_rule` carries that column on a registered object."
  - Two other registered objects carry the same read-only `managed_by` select (platform / package / admin):
    - `sys_email_template`, declared at `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email-template.object.ts` :166 and registered by `plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts` :371;
    - `sys_webhook`, declared at `plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts` :269 and registered by `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts` :182.
  - The `a581c57eae` note two lines below already states the fact with the right scope: "of the three provenance-column objects only `sys_sharing_rule` remains".
  - **Remedy:** scope the sentence ("Of the three objects named, only `sys_sharing_rule` is still registered"), or drop the clause.
  - It blocks because the card's acceptance is that every line it names is true of `main`, and the maintainer approves this text on this record.
- **B (non-blocking). More prose still describes the gate as live.** The PR hands only two comments to 8-post; these also remain:
  - `security-plugin.ts` :6151, in the same file: the preview docblock lists "the ADR-0090 D5/D9 audience-anchor binding guard" among the pre-resolution gates that run;
  - `objectql/src/engine.ts` :5518–5519, the same list;
  - `engine.ts` :8857–8859 and `objectql/src/integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts` :375: "the audience-anchor gate has to resolve that permission set";
  - `lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` :37: "held by the runtime's own `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(set, 'guest')` gate";
  - `qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts` :578, which names `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` as a live, unfiltered write gate.

  8-post was told to keep the gate (6161961558, item 1), so its sweep will not have taken these. They need a named carrier.
- **C (non-blocking). Two more gates are dead for the same reason.** The PR names `assertSystemRowWriteGate`. Also unreachable: `assertCuratedCapabilityNameGate` (`sys_capability` only) and `assertPackageManagedWriteGate` (`sys_permission_set` only). 8-post's carry-over lists "the four gates"; the seat should confirm these two are among them.
- **D (note). Landing order.** 8-post edits the lines next to the removed call and method in `security-plugin.ts`, so whichever PR lands second needs a re-merge.

### ② Semver level

`patch` agrees with the changeset (`.changeset/23403-audience-anchor-binding-gate-retired.md`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`).

- The gate was a private method of the exported `SecurityPlugin`, and the package's `exports` cannot reach it.
- The two imports removed were internal.
- No export or signature changes. Behaviour does not change either, because the code was unreachable.
- `Check Changeset` succeeded on the head, and the changeset text is accurate.
- Nothing under `packages/spec/src/**` is touched, so `Clause-②: no` is right. The review is owed only because governed text (`docs/adr/**`) changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's flags.** `open_questions` and `deviations` are both empty, so there is nothing to answer.
  - Out-of-scope finding 1, `assertSystemRowWriteGate`, belongs with 8-post's residue. Agreed; see C.
  - Out-of-scope finding 2, the prose list, is incomplete; see B.
- **Boundaries.** The diff crosses no repository boundary, no app/platform boundary and no published-contract boundary. Item 5 cites objectui's pin that a guest row offers no Accept; this diff does not affect it.
- **NOT MEASURED: dogfood and the CLI tier.** Acceptable for this diff.
  - The engine refuses an unregistered object before the middleware runs, so no dogfood scenario could reach the removed code.
  - The CLI's organization-ownership ceremony reads the legacy bindings table outside the engine middleware.
  - CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate` succeeded on the head; its shards were skipped by the path filter.
- **Check-runs on `bd13bf7808`:** all 40 completed: 34 success, 6 skipped (opt-in pack smoke, docs build, console pin, the dogfood shards, the CLI dogfood, temporal conformance), 0 red, none still running. That includes `Test Core` (1/6 to 6/6), `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check`.
  - The earlier head `59761d4a71` showed 7 cancelled runs and 1 failure. The failure was `TypeScript Type Check`: "type-check lane `typecheck-workspace` concluded `cancelled`". They are the concurrency cancellation from when the head moved, and none of them is on this head.

FAIL rests on finding A alone. If A is fixed and nothing else moves, a delta review of the new head should be able to pass it.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-14T07:12Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript (opus). The reviewer made reads, `git fetch` into review refs, REST GETs, and record writes only. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat takes the verdict as FAIL, on finding A only.
- **The fix:** the dev restates the ADR-0103 sentence (about :53–54). It says only that, of the three objects it names, `sys_sharing_rule` alone is still registered. `sys_email_template` and `sys_webhook` also carry `managed_by`.
- **Then:** a delta review on the new head, and the Tier H kit for the maintainer's approval.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0f2d82aebdc78811b39b099d947ff204851324a7`
Local-runs: none

PR #23412, card #23403 (Tier H by path, `docs/adr/**`). Served in-seat at the contract tier by the director seat (summon #37) on the maintainer's word 「23412 你帮我做一轮fable复审」, 2026-10-14T07:41Z. The head is the PR's current head `0f2d82aebd`: `59761d4a71` (the change), `bd13bf7808` (main `5656c5638a` merged, which carries 7a `dac99c2277`), `0f2d82aebd` (ADR-0103's sentence restated, the fix for finding A of the prior record 6162991283). This is the newest record naming this head; the prior record names `bd13bf7808` and was adopted from a default-tier reviewer, so it does not stand for the current head on its own. Read for this record: the net diff (8 files, +54/−142), the card, the dev report 6162484475 and comment 6162563147, the prior record, ADR-0131 D10/D13, and the head's check-runs. Every claim below was re-read on `origin/main` `5656c5638` from this seat, independently of the prior record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The gate is dead on `main` and is removed whole.** `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` returned unless `opCtx.object === 'sys_position_permission_set'`. No `name: 'sys_position_permission_set'` registration exists in `packages/**` on `main` (stage 8, `66949b7729`, retired the four catalog row objects; the only definition left is a test kit), and the engine resolves the object name before the middleware runs, so no write reaches the gate. The diff removes the one call (`security-plugin.ts` :2528 on `main`), the private method (:6821–6890), its three direct-call cases, and the two imports with no other use in the file (`describeAnchorForbiddenBits`, `AnchorBindingContext`); `readDeclaredCapabilityContext` keeps its other use (:4779, `declareEveryone`). A grep of `main` finds no other code caller: the remaining names are prose (ADR-0138, `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts:360`, `qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:578`, a CHANGELOG). Correct.
2. **No ADR-0090 D9 guarantee is lost.** `describeAnchorForbiddenBits` still runs where an `everyone` binding is made: `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` :512 (the derivation) and :865 (confirm), and at authoring time in `lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` :777. The `guest` tier has no caller because no door binds a set to `guest`; that is the state #23267's ruling C (6159279205) left on purpose (the bind door is follow-up F4). ADR-0138's map row moving to "enforced for `everyone`; `guest`: follow-up F4" is the true status, not a new decision. Correct.
3. **ADR-0103 (:50–59), the fixed sentence.** `SYSTEM_ROW_PROVENANCE` holds `sys_position` and `sys_capability` only (:797–); `git log -S` over the file's history shows `sys_sharing_rule` was never a key of that map, so "never `sys_sharing_rule`" is true; `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-provenance.ts` stamps `customized` instead of refusing; of the three objects the aside names, only `sys_sharing_rule` is registered on `main` (`sys-sharing-rule.object.ts:29`).
